newsitem.title: USA: Air Force chief sees no U.S. blame in explosion.
newsitem.headline: Air Force chief sees no U.S. blame in explosion.

text.p: The Air Force's top general said on Tuesday he found no U.S. military blame in the Saudi bombing that killed 19 U.S. servicemen and said commanders should not be punished just to take someone's scalp.

"It is criminal for us to try and hold somebody accountable or to discipline somebody for political correctness or because the media has created a frenzy based on partial information and not the full facts," Air Force Chief of Staff Gen. Ronald Fogleman said at a Senate hearing.

The Air Force is reviewing whether Brig. Gen. Terryl Schwalier, who was commander of U.S. air operations in Saudi Arabia, or any other commander should be punished for not doing enough to protect U.S. troops before the truck bombing last June that ripped open a U.S. military housing complex.

Fogleman said at the Senate Armed Services Committee hearing that U.S. commanders had ordered 137 security measures before the bombing and that his own review found no justification for punishement of any of them.
He said unfair punishment of those commanders would demoralise other U.S. commanders throughout the military.

"If they despite their absolute best efforts are targeted by somebody in an act of war and somebody is killed and no matter what they have done this town, this city, this climate cries for their scalp, I hate to think about what that will do for the force," Fogleman said.

A scathing Pentagon report concluded that senior officers were responsible for the high number of servicemen killed and wounded by the bombing because they had not done enough to protect American troops from attack.
But a subsequent Air Force report, which has not been officially released, absolved Schwalier and other senior officers of any blame, saying they did all they could.

The Air Force announced last month it had delayed Schwalier's promotion to major general until it completes the review of whether any U.S. commander should be punished. Fogleman said the review should be completed early in March.

U.S. officials have complained Saudi Arabia is not sharing enough information about its investigation of the bombing. But Saudi Defence Minister Prince Sultan, in Washington for a visit, said on Tuesday he hoped to allay such concerns.
